doc.title: Alicia Olatuja interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 9, 2018

title: Audience question: influences, 'Intuition' album and 'Over the Rainbow'
summary: She describes her album of women composers and the arrangement of 'Somewhere Over the Rainbow' with Christian Sands.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I see. Do we have a question from the audience? Someone want to ask?
Yes, I’m just curious, do you ever take, do you ever look at like contemporary artists and like incorporate bits into your own style from even household names like Beyoncé like you mentioned?

Well I mean it’s great that you mention that because the next album that I just recorded is actually called “Intuition, Songs from the Minds of Women” and it’s celebrating and championing women composers. And I use, I collected a bunch of different songs from women composers of all the genres and backgrounds, from Joni Mitchell to Imogen Heap to Sade, to my student. Like, as well as my own songs as well. But I think hearing the through line of the experience, the human experience is what I’m really going after. I’m really trying to capture that. Because music is all about unifying us above our race and religion and political point of views, and I think that can’t be boxed in a genre and you can’t say I refuse to be influenced by this person, because they, whatever reason. So I’m influenced by a lot of different musicians and artists and I’m going to do one of those tunes tonight so hopefully you’ll recognize it. But anyway, it’s a different arrangement but it’s pretty cool.
Yeah I was just listening to your version of “Somewhere Over the Rainbow.” Where do you come up with that?

Well I actually — half of it a friend of mine, Christian Sands, he had arranged that for his trio. And it was just the same eight bars that were looping. And I was like, “Oh how lovely.” But it was just the song [sings] it was not the [sings] some day I wish upon a star. So then we sat down and I said you know I really want to do that part of the song but we have to build to that. I can’t just do nothing for eight bars. And then I really wanted to stretch the line and stretch the text. And yeah, we just kind of made it flow, and yeah, I really like it. It’s a tough sing, I like it.
A tough sing. I like that phrase.
